edits.new: A valid counterexample refutes that direction without further restriction tests. A full-coverage justification must give a concise restriction audit: first each applicable identity or consumer condition expressly required by the parent but absent from the child's explicit wording, then other applicable parent conditions absent from that wording. For each, name the condition, describe a concrete potential child case attempting to violate it, and resolve admission under the whole child and exclusion from every parent alternative or permitted connection. If the attempt fails, identify the contradictory child wording or necessary implication, or the covering parent alternative or connection. Merely naming a condition or asserting that it necessarily holds is not its concrete test. For a particular-entity child, establish needed properties without assigning unknown facts. Customary cases and one covered example do not establish universal coverage.
edits.old: A valid counterexample refutes that direction without further restriction tests. Before any full-coverage conclusion, explicitly test each applicable parent identity or consumer restriction absent from the child's explicit wording: put an outside-class entity in the constrained role and adjudicate the concrete case against the whole child and all parent alternatives and permitted connections. Identify any necessary implication excluding it.
